question: For the D.C. Council in recent Council Periods: (1) how many bills are introduced per two-year period, and how many permanent acts, emergency acts and temporary acts are enacted; (2) how many legislative meetings it holds per year, and in which months it recesses; (3) the rough subject mix of enacted permanent acts (ceremonial and naming, land and property dispositions, public safety, housing, taxes and budget support, health, education, government operations); (4) what share of introduced bills reach a first-reading vote; (5) how often a final vote is not unanimous, and how often an act fails a vote on the floor rather than dying in committee.
requestedBy: Codex's overnight dispatch (item 12d, D.C. Council ordinances missing), relayed by the coordinator at 3:34 a.m. Eastern on September 23, 2026; filed by the D.C. Council thread

sourcesChecked.source: D.C. Code §§ 1-204.04, 1-204.12 and 1-206.02, locked in data/source/municipal-governance/raw from the Council's law-xml-codified repository
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: The statute sets procedure, not volume, calendar or subject mix.

title: How much legislation the D.C. Council takes up, and on what
usableAnswer: Counts per Council Period for (1), a meeting calendar for (2), a subject table for (3), and two or three shares for (4) and (5), each marked measured or estimated.
whyItMatters: In play the Council sits every 14 days, one member introduces one act at each sitting on a question from the game's policy catalog, and each member's ballot is a game-authored stand-in (src/simulation/dc-council-sittings.ts). A year from January 5, 2026 gave 25 acts and 11 laws; about half failed on the floor, which is likely far too many. Every one of those numbers is a placeholder.
